merged_body: Per-arch register tables in native/angr/src/arch/{amd64,x86,arm,arm64,mips}.rs use CANONICAL: &[RegEntry] + ALIASES: &[RegEntry] const slices, where RegEntry = (name, offset, size_bytes). The lookup_register_{offset,size,name} helpers in arch/mod.rs and the impl_arch_registers!(canonical, aliases, names) macro drive the trait methods. CANONICAL drives register_name(offset) reverse lookups (one canonical name per offset); ALIASES holds sub-register names sharing an offset (e.g., 'eax' aliases 'rax' on amd64) and is consulted only by name->offset/size forward lookups. To add a new register: add ONE row in CANONICAL (if reverse-mappable) or ALIASES (if just a forward alias). The (name, offset, size) triplet is now a single source of truth. ARM canonical uses sp/lr/pc (not r13/r14/r15t); ARM64 uses fp/lr/sp (not x29/x30/xsp); MIPS uses ABI mnemonics (zero/at/v0/...) not numeric rN. MIPS64 register_name is intentionally narrow (only zero/v0/a0/sp/fp/ra/pc reverse-mappable) — preserved bug-for-bug. Arch trait methods (sp_offset, ip_offset, return_register, syscall_num_offset) live alongside the tables. NEVER hand-code 'match VexArch { ... => (offset, size) }' tables in callers — they will silently drift. Always reach data through self.registers.arch() or arch_from_vex(arch).<method>(). If a needed lookup isn't on the trait, add a trait method, don't duplicate the match.

merged_body: Pattern for documenting cross-cutting bd-memory invariants into rustdoc (established angr-a2br.1.1-1.4, commits 717583fa3 / 3bfe94c44, 2026-06-01): (1) module-header 'Lineage + solver invariants' section enumerates each invariant in its own paragraph with the bd-memory key in backticks and a one-line failure mode it prevents — the first surface a reader hits via cargo doc. (2) Field-level rustdoc carries load-bearing-shape callouts (e.g., the Mutex<Option<Arc<Mutex<...>>>> 'why two layers' paragraph citing invariant-v5a5-lineage-mutex-shape). (3) Mutating methods (fork, set_use_shared_lineage_solver, _add_state) get 'Cross-cutting invariants enforced here' subsections naming each bd memory key. (4) Debug_asserts only where they restate a precondition tautologically true today (fork-time bare_z3_push_depth==0, child_id > parent_id, fork ID != source ID); asserts that would only catch a future refactor mistake are the right granularity for invariant documentation. (5) When an invariant is enforced on a Rust call_* method (e.g., call_on_hook ok_or_else) but the rule lives in Python (e.g., four-export-paths), number the Rust invariants 1-N so Python-side dispatchers can cross-ref by stable identifier (callbacks.rs module invariant 4). (6) For god-objects with multiple caches (claripy_bridge.rs), layer per-cache rustdoc + a cross-cutting numbered block (C1-C6) in the same file; Python-side counterparts get a single 'see state.rs I3/I4/I5/I6' pointer to avoid 3-way duplication. (7) When an invariant lives mostly on the Python side, document it as a Python-only cross-ref at the Rust enforcement site (or NEAR-enforcement field) with short 'See module-level X' rather than prose duplication.
